problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}+1,\,{t}^{2}-1,\,2t⟩$, use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature as a function of $t.$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩=⟨2t,\,2t,\,2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4(2{t}^{2}+1)} \\  & =2\sqrt{2{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the second derivative ${r}^{″}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩=⟨2,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the cross-product:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t) & =⟨2t,2t,2⟩\times ⟨2,2,0⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 2t & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2t & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2t & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2t & 2t \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-4i+4j+(4t-4t)k \\  & =-4\,i+4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the magnitude of the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{32} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{{[2\sqrt{2{t}^{2}+1}]}^{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2(2{t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
